prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK’s 2024 “Contract with You” presents itself as a common-sense alternative to Conservatives and Labour, arguing Britain faces crises in immigration, public services, cost of living, energy and trust in institutions. It frames Brexit as a missed opportunity and proposes rapid, large-scale reforms within 100 days and beyond.

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration; stop small boats by leaving the ECHR, detaining and deporting illegal arrivals, and returning boats to France.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use; cut management waste; offer tax breaks to retain/attract staff; use independent capacity.
- Make work pay: raise income tax threshold to £20,000; lift higher rate to £70,000.
- Cut and stabilise energy bills: scrap Net Zero and green levies; expand domestic oil and gas.
- Restore law and order and protect British culture, identity and values.

Key policies
- Immigration: bar student dependants; no legal aid for non-citizens; rapid offshore processing; five-year residency/work to access benefits; immediate deportation of foreign criminals; employer immigration tax (20% NI on foreign workers, exempt essential health/care and very small firms).
- Government waste: end interest on QE reserves paid to banks; 5% efficiency savings across departments; halve foreign aid; cut EU-era red tape; boost HMRC tax collection.
- Personal economy: cut fuel duty by 20p; remove VAT on energy and green levies; slash stamp duty (0% to £750k); restore tax-free shopping; raise IHT threshold to £2m (20% above that).
- Business: lift corporation tax threshold to £100k; cut main rate to 20%, then 15% (year 3); abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k; abolish business rates for high-street SMEs and offset with a 4% online delivery tax; streamline planning; ease hiring/firing and simplify the tax code.
- NHS: zero basic-rate income tax for NHS/social care staff for three years; end training caps; student fee write-offs tied to service; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance; NHS vouchers if waits exceed targets; expand weekend operating; reduce managers and PFI costs; “Pharmacy First”.
- Energy/Net Zero: scrap Net Zero and renewable subsidies via equivalent taxes; fast-track North Sea and shale; expand SMRs and other tech.
- Policing/Justice: recruit 40,000 officers; zero tolerance policing; expand stop-and-search; tougher drug/crime penalties; £2bn justice boost; 10,000 new prison places; redefine hate crime.
- Education: “patriotic curriculum”; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap student loan interest; stricter university standards and free speech enforcement.
- Benefits: tighter assessments; two-strike job rule within four months; focus on 16–34s back to work.
- Brexit/constitution/culture: scrap retained EU law and the Windsor Framework; leave ECHR; reform House of Lords and postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights; scrap BBC licence; replace Equalities Act; free speech bill; oppose WHO treaty, WEF influence and CBDC.
- Defence: raise spending to 2.5% GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rise; veterans department; procurement reform.
- Housing: speed brownfield building; prioritise locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest relief for landlords; scrap Renters’ Reform Bill.
- Families/transport/agriculture/fishing/utilities: marriage tax allowance (when affordable); front-load child benefit; single-sex spaces; scrap HS2; ban ULEZ/LTNs; mixed public/pension-fund ownership of utilities; more farm support; rebuild fishing; social care commission.

Funding (claimed)
- Savings up to £150bn/year: £50bn departmental efficiencies; £35bn QE interest halt; £30bn Net Zero/energy; £15bn benefits; £6bn aid; £4bn employer immigration tax; plus £10bn/year from 1% extra growth. Total potential £160bn/year vs total policy costs of £141bn/year.
</text>
